Initiative_Name: Adopt a net-zero buildings plan
Title: Whitbread ESG Report
Narrative:
Hotels & Restaurants: Portfolio net-zero plan – Whitbread
Rolling out low-carbon rooms across the estate delivered 2,300 low-carbon rooms and a 63% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions intensity versus 2016/17. [1]

QSR: Net-zero restaurant blueprint – McDonald’s Market Drayton
McDonald’s replaced conventional man-made insulation with British sheep wool, used 250 m² of cladding made from recycled IT and white goods, and installed more than 1,000 kerbs made from 182 recycled plastic bottles each instead of conventional concrete kerbs. Two wind turbines and 92 m² of solar panels generate 60,000 kWh per year, while each recycled kerb has a 25 kgCO₂ lower footprint than a concrete equivalent. [2]

Initiative_Name: Measure and verify building energy performance
Title: Optimised Radisson Blu Case Study
Narrative:
Hotels: Integrated HVAC, BEMS and CHP optimisation – Radisson Blu
The 218-room hotel had individually commissioned HVAC, BEMS, absorption-chiller and 285 kW bio-oil CHP systems that were not operating as one coordinated system. Existing submeters were connected to the Trend BEMS, half-hourly data established the baseline, analytics identified anomalies, and the CHP, boilers and electric and absorption chillers were then retuned and continuously recommissioned, reducing total energy by 30%, electricity by 17% and gas by 41% with payback under 12 months. [1]

Leased Buildings: Owner-occupier energy management – York House
The landlord and occupier formed an Environmental Management Group, installed automatic 15-minute energy monitoring, separated landlord-controlled common-area and HVAC loads from occupier-controlled loads, and agreed an annual Environmental Action Plan with named responsibilities. Annual energy fell by 1.1 million kWh, saving £63,000 and 416 tCO₂; landlord-controlled energy fell 32% and occupier-controlled energy fell 9%. [2]

Initiative_Name: Optimise and upgrade HVAC systems and controls
Title: Energy Technology List Coplow Centre Case
Narrative:
Pubs / Community Hospitality: Heating-control recommissioning – Coplow Centre
The venue’s hall, meeting rooms, bar and commercial kitchen previously relied on costly heating with long warm-up times and limited control. A HeatingSave control system was installed to coordinate the boiler, radiant heater and solar system, link operating schedules to room bookings and occupancy sensors, and use self-learning optimum-start control, reducing the gas bill by 51% and warm-up time by 90%. [1]

Hotels: Whole-building HVAC and BEMS recommissioning – Radisson Blu
Rather than replacing the plant, the hotel used existing submeters and half-hourly BEMS data to diagnose poor interaction between HVAC, a 285 kW bio-oil CHP, boilers, an absorption chiller and electric chillers. Coordinating and continuously retuning these systems reduced total energy by 30%, electricity by 17% and gas by 41%, with payback under 12 months. [2]

Hotels / Resorts: Air-cooled to water-cooled chiller replacement – Commercial Resort, Bogor
The five-floor resort and convention centre has 7,738 m² of conditioned space covering its lobby, ballrooms, meeting rooms, restaurants and guestrooms. Three fixed-speed McQuay air-cooled screw chillers installed in 1999, each rated at 155 TR (545.11 kW), COP 5.71 and IPLV 3.82, were replaced in 2020 by two fixed-speed TICA water-cooled screw chillers, each rated at 185 TR (650.62 kW), COP 6.07 and IPLV 5.59. Modelled and measured post-installation performance showed 17.5% lower energy consumption, 2,860 tCO₂e lower annual emissions and 13.4% lower life-cycle cost while maintaining indoor comfort. [3]

QSR: Rooftop HVAC and kitchen-hood redesign – Wendy’s
At two rebuilt restaurants in Mobile, Alabama, the control site used two high-efficiency rooftop units plus a dedicated make-up-air unit, while the upgraded site paired new lower-airflow kitchen hoods with two Trane Voyager rooftop units using eFlex variable-speed compressors. Over the first 8 months, total energy fell 24% at the upgraded site versus 13% at the control; a later Columbus retrofit cut rooftop-unit energy by more than 60% and total restaurant energy by more than 10%. [4]

Initiative_Name: Install smart draught beverage dispense systems
Title: Lisini Pub Co SmartDispense case, Scottish Licensed Trade News
Narrative:
Pubs / Hotels – Six-Week SmartDispense Rollout – Lisini Pub Co [1]
Lisini installed HEINEKEN SmartDispense across its venues after engaging its maintenance team, supplier and independent trade advisers. The system replaced frequent manual line cleaning with a supplier-managed six-week cycle, reduced beer, water and chemical losses, simplified keg changes and added a 54-point technical check at each service. Lisini’s procurement manager estimates annual savings above £40,000 across the group, with further savings from lower cellar-cooling energy.

Pubs – SmartDispense Across 200 Star Pubs [2]
Star Pubs analysed 200 installations where SmartDispense was the only reported operational change. Published results showed an 8% sales uplift, around 4,500 litres of water and 33 litres of cleaning chemical saved per pub each year, 3% more beer reaching the glass and 3% less entering drip trays. Across the estate, Star reported £5 million of additional annual value.

Hotels / Leisure – Reduced Line-Cleaning Waste – Bluestone National Park Resort [3]
Bluestone moved routine line cleaning to the SmartDispense service and reported average savings of 45 pints and 3 staff hours per bar each week after two years. This equates to approximately 2,340 pints and 156 staff hours per bar annually while maintaining clean lines and consistent beer quality.

Experiential Leisure – Enclosed Keg-to-Glass Dispense – Crucible Corner, Sheffield [4]
The theatre venue installed Carlsberg’s enclosed, continuously chilled Quality Dispense System. During its first three months, the team cleaned the lines only three times while reporting consistently crisp product quality. The wider system extends cleaning from weekly to four-weekly, while CQDS Plus can reach ten weeks; Carlsberg reports average venue water savings of 4,000 litres and at least 30% lower cooler energy costs.

Hotels / Leisure – Fobbing Reduction – Nailcote Hall Hotel, Golf & Country Club [5]
Nailcote Hall replaced its standard dispense setup with Carlsberg’s continuously chilled system. The food and beverage manager reported that fobbing was almost eliminated, wastage was near zero and four-weekly cleaning substantially reduced beer sent to drain while maintaining product quality.

Initiative_Name: Install timer controls across eligible equipment
Title: The Folly Energy Saving Recommendations Report
Narrative:
Restaurant / Bar – Scheduling a 9.5 kW Hot-Water Boiler – The Folly, Oxford [1]
A 9.5 kW domestic hot-water boiler was found operating 24 hours a day. The audit recommended a 7-day timer that starts the boiler 30 minutes before demand and switches it off from midnight to 9am. The audit summary estimated £68 implementation cost, 683 kWh and £18 annual saving, approximately 0.13 tCO2e avoided and a 3.8-year payback.

Restaurant – Staggered Kitchen Fire-Up and Shutdown – UK Restaurant [2]
An energy specialist fixed a broken kitchen-extraction timer, delayed extract start until 10am, switched the glasswasher on later, turned the cutlery polisher off between uses, shut equipment down during quiet service and introduced a gradual close-down routine. The combined scheduling and behavioural package saved £18,000 and 28 tCO2 annually; the result is a bundled operational saving rather than a timer-only claim.

Pub – Smart Cellar Cooler Timers – Stonegate Pub Company [3]
Following a successful trial, Stonegate rolled cellar controls out to 550 sites. Cellar Manager controls reduced main cellar-cooler energy by up to 30%, while Smart Python Timers were programmed to each pub's opening hours and switched remote coolers off overnight, delivering a further 25% energy reduction while maintaining product quality.

Hotel / Leisure – 15-Minute Whirlpool-Blower Run-Back Timer – Hotel Case [4]
A 3 kW whirlpool blower drawing approximately 2.5 kW was operating from 8am to midnight. A 15-minute wind-up timer was estimated to reduce annual runtime by 4,380 hours, or 75%, save 11,000 kWh a year and achieve payback in under one month.

QSR – Automated Scheduling for Walk-Ins, HVAC and Lighting – National Hamburger Chain [5]
A national hamburger QSR tested adaptive walk-in controls, smart thermostat schedules and lighting controls at three locations over six weeks. The supplier-reported results showed energy reductions of up to 27% for walk-ins, 43% for HVAC and 8% for lighting, demonstrating the broader opportunity to automate equipment schedules beyond boilers.

Initiative_Name: Optimise fans and pumps with variable-speed drives, efficient motors and demand controls
Title: Energy Technology List Wetherspoon Case
Narrative:
Pubs: Demand-controlled kitchen ventilation – Wetherspoon Jack Fairman, Horley
The pub integrated the ETL-listed Quintex CHEETAH demand-control system with its HVAC controls. Temperature, optical and flow sensors detect heat, steam and smoke and adjust extract and supply fan speed so ventilation only runs at the level required by cooking demand. Fan energy fell by 69%, saving 36,167 kWh, £9,041 and 8.1 tCO₂ per year with 1.88-year payback; a 654-site rollout reportedly saved more than 7 million kWh and £1.47 million annually. [1]

QSR: Variable-speed rooftop HVAC – Wendy’s
Wendy’s combined lower-airflow kitchen hoods with Trane Voyager rooftop units using eFlex variable-speed compressors, allowing cooling and fan output to follow actual load instead of operating at fixed capacity. A Columbus retrofit used more than 60% less rooftop-unit energy in the first 2 months and reduced total restaurant energy by more than 10%; the design became a standard option for new company and franchise sites. [2]

Leisure: Variable-speed pool circulation – Leicester
Five variable-speed drives were fitted to swimming-pool circulation plant so pump speed could be reduced when full flow was not required, replacing fixed-speed operation. The installation saved 240,000 kWh per year, equal to 48,000 kWh per VSD, with 1.11-year payback and no measurable decline in water quality. [3]

Initiative_Name: Recover and reuse waste heat from refrigeration, cooking or wastewater
Title: UK Government Yeo Valley Heat Recovery Case
Narrative:
Food Production: Refrigeration heat recovery – Yeo Valley
The dairy’s refrigeration system rejected condenser heat to air while cleaning water was heated by steam from an 85%-efficient natural-gas boiler. Yeo Valley installed a CO₂ refrigeration plant with an integral 250 kW plate heat exchanger, controls, protection and insulated storage linked to the existing hot-water ring main, raising water from 10°C to 65°C and recovering 943 MWh per year; the system cost more than £64,000 before a 30% grant, offsets nearly £22,000 of gas cost and avoids 175 tCO₂e annually with about 2-year payback. [1]

QSR: Kitchen-exhaust heat recovery pilot – Burger King Welwyn Garden City
Burger King installed Enjay exhaust heat recovery on a new restaurant where roughly 1 m³/s of hot, moist and contaminated kitchen exhaust would otherwise be discharged outdoors. The pilot used site simulation, measured performance and comparison with similar restaurants to test the business case; the pre-installation model estimated around 80,000 kWh of recoverable heat per restaurant per year, with actual performance to be validated through monitoring. [2]

Initiative_Name: Upgrade boiler burner controls and balance heat-distribution systems
Title: Energy Technology List Leadenhall Autoflame Case
Narrative:
Commercial Buildings: Boiler burner controls – Leadenhall Building
The building upgraded ageing boiler-burner controls with Autoflame Mini Mk8 MM micro-modulating controllers, which continuously adjust the fuel-air ratio instead of relying on less precise conventional burner control. The upgrade saved £60,000 and 180 tCO₂ per year with a 2-year ROI. [1]

Healthcare: Boiler burner controls – NHS site
An NHS site applied the same micro-modulating burner-control technology to ageing and unreliable boiler plant, improving combustion control and reducing fuel cost by 7.03%, carbon emissions by 15.14% and NOx by more than 59%. [2]

Initiative_Name: Upgrade domestic hot-water generation, storage and circulation controls
Title: Minnesota Hotel DHW Recirculation Study
Narrative:
Hotels: Demand-based hot-water recirculation – Three-hotel field study
Demand-based circulation controls reduced water-heating energy by 9.9%–15.9% and pump electricity by 70%–93% in the two fully measured hotels, with 1.8–2.1-year payback. [1]

Hotels: DHW monitoring and rapid fault response – Hampton Inn & Suites Boston
Continuous temperature monitoring identified an overnight water-heater trip; resetting the burner restored normal hot-water service within 1 hour before guests were affected. [2]

Initiative_Name: Automate shutdown of non-HVAC, non-lighting equipment outside operating hours
Title: U.S. GSA Advanced Power Strips Findings
Narrative:
International: Automated plug-load shutdown – GSA facilities
Advanced power strips and schedule controls reduced plug loads by 48% on average, including nearly 50% in kitchens and printer rooms; kitchen applications achieved 0.7-year payback. [1]

Restaurants: Off-peak kitchen-equipment shutdown – Shari’s Café & Pies
Shutdown checklists for second cook lines and broiler burners supported a wider equipment-use programme that cut electricity by 6%, gas by 25% and water by more than 40% between 2008 and 2015. [2]

Initiative_Name: Implement power management for small-power, IT and server-room equipment
Title: U.S. DOE CCAC Computer Power Management
Narrative:
International: Computer power management – Community College of Allegheny County
Applying central power-management settings reduced electricity use by 74%, from 33 kWh to 9 kWh per computer per month, saving 288 kWh per computer per year. [1]

International: Smart control of printers and small-power loads – UC San Diego
Static schedules cut plug-load energy by 38%–66%; print-server controls cut printer energy by 86%, and scheduled water dispensers cut energy by 32% with three-year payback. [2]

Initiative_Name: Upgrade lift and escalator drives and controls
Title: ACEEE Hyatt Place Elevator Case
Narrative:
Hotels: Regenerative lift modernisation – Hyatt Place Waikiki Beach
Replacing lift machines and controls with permanent-magnet motors, destination software and regenerative drives reduced lift electricity use by 56% while improving reliability and ride quality. [1]

Hotels: Regenerative lift drives – Emily Morgan Hotel
Installing regenerative lift drives reduced watt-hours by 45% and peak electrical demand by 31%. [2]

Initiative_Name: Optimise swimming-pool circulation, heating, covers and backwashing
Title: Leicester City Council Pool VSD Case
Narrative:
Leisure: Variable-speed pool circulation – Leicester
Five variable-speed drives replaced fixed-speed operation on swimming-pool circulation plant, allowing pump flow to match actual filtration demand rather than running continuously at full speed. The installation saved 240,000 kWh per year, equal to 48,000 kWh per VSD, with no measurable deterioration in pool-water quality and 1.11-year payback. [1]

Hotels: Swimming-pool heat pump – City-centre rooftop pool
The pool-heating system used a heat pump instead of relying solely on direct electric or gas-boiler heat. Measured operation delivered 49.1 MWh of heat from 24.6 MWh of electricity at an average COP of 2.0, saving 26.5–32.5 MWh per heating season versus the alternative boiler baselines. [2]

Initiative_Name: Replace high-GWP refrigerants with lower-GWP alternatives during planned plant intervention
Title: CCAC Low-GWP Commercial Refrigeration Cases
Narrative:
International Retail Food: Low-GWP CO₂ refrigeration – Sobeys
Sobeys’ transcritical CO₂ systems with heat reclaim delivered 0%–15% lower installation cost, 50% lower maintenance cost, 75%–85% lower heating cost and under three-year payback in the cited cases. [1]

International Retail Food: CO₂ secondary-loop refrigeration – Loblaw Scarborough
A CO₂ secondary loop with subcooling, floating head pressure and heat recovery used 23% less energy and reduced GHG emissions by 59%, equal to 2,700 tCO₂e, versus a similar conventional supermarket. [2]

Initiative_Name: Install refrigerant leak detection and implement rapid repair
Title: Shropshire Commercial Refrigeration Guide
Narrative:
Commercial Refrigeration: Leak detection and rapid repair benchmark
Published refrigeration guidance indicates leaking systems can be 11% less efficient, while detection and repair can reduce energy cost by up to 15%; indicative payback is 2–3 years for small leaks and under one year for large leaks. [1]

International Food Retail: Continuous refrigerant leak detection – Spanish grocery chain
Installing continuous leak detection across 5 stores reduced refrigerant leakage by 71% and leak-location time by 90% within 4 weeks. [2]

Initiative_Name: Maintain a governed refrigerant inventory and leakage record
Title: Facilio HelloFresh Refrigerant Compliance Case
Narrative:
Food Production: Central refrigerant compliance tracking – HelloFresh
HelloFresh centralised refrigerant tracking across food-production facilities, using instant triggers to remove delays between detection and action and accelerate closure of refrigerant events. [1]

International Food Retail: Refrigerant analytics and compliance records – Woolworths
Connecting refrigeration data across more than 1,200 stores automated compliance logs and prioritised faults, reducing refrigerant leaks by 37%, avoiding 1,885 service calls and cutting Scope 1 emissions by 27%. [2]

Initiative_Name: Recover refrigerants at equipment end of life and document transfer
Title: UK Government WEEE Refrigerant Recovery Guidance
Narrative:
UK Treatment Benchmark: End-of-life refrigerant recovery – WEEE plants
UK guidance requires treatment systems to recover at least 90% of refrigerant, while dedicated treatment plant is designed to remove and collect more than 99%. [1]

International: End-of-life R-12 recovery and destruction – University of Rochester
Recovering and destroying 23,635 lb of R-12 from 2 retired chillers avoided 103,650 tCO₂e and generated a project credit from the recovered refrigerant. [2]

Initiative_Name: Upgrade refrigeration equipment, doors, seals, fans and controls
Title: Energy Technology List Greene King Case
Narrative:
Pubs: Efficient bottle-cooler replacement – Greene King Punch and Judy
The pub replaced 8 mixed-manufacturer, older-generation double-door bottle coolers consuming 4.71 kWh per unit per day with ETL-listed Rhino units selected for rapid pull-down and lower energy use. The new coolers consume 0.81 kWh per unit per day, saving about £2,500 per year at 25p/kWh; reported fan life increased from about 4 years to nearly 8 years, with around £300 of service call-outs avoided over an appliance life. [1]

Food Retail: Door-fronted refrigeration – Washingpool Farm Shop
Three open-fronted refrigerated cabinets were replaced with door-fronted units to reduce cold-air loss into the shop. The £30,889 project was estimated to reduce refrigeration energy by 61%, saving about 54,000 kWh, £15,000 and 28 tCO₂e per year. [2]

Initiative_Name: Adopt a validated warmer freezer setpoint where product and food-safety rules allow
Title: IESO Freezer Setpoint Research Study
Narrative:
International Restaurants / Hotels: Warmer freezer setpoint trial – IESO
Raising freezer setpoints from −18°C to −15°C across more than 24 restaurant and hotel freezers reduced freezer energy use by 10% on average, with almost all foods remaining safe and without loss of quality. [1]

Initiative_Name: Phase out fossil-fuelled patio heaters and avoid unnecessary outdoor heating
Title: Energy Saving Trust Outdoor Heating Comparison
Narrative:
Hospitality Reference: Targeted electric outdoor heating – Energy Saving Trust
The published comparison indicates targeted electric infrared heating can reduce running cost by 66.7% versus gas patio heating for the same stated area and duration, while directing heat toward people and objects. [1]

Initiative_Name: Conduct whole-life carbon assessments for major capital projects
Title: UKGBC Entopia Building Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Whole-life carbon assessment – Entopia Building
Whole-life carbon assessment was used to compare deep retrofit with conventional refurbishment, prioritising retention of the existing structure rather than demolition and replacement. The selected design is expected to save 80% of whole-life carbon versus a standard refurbishment, while structural retention avoided about 60% of embodied carbon. [1]

QSR: Net-zero construction benchmark – McDonald’s Market Drayton
McDonald’s tested specific lower-carbon substitutions rather than relying on a generic green-building label: sheep wool replaced man-made insulation, 250 m² of external cladding was made from recycled IT and white goods, and more than 1,000 kerbs were made from recycled bottles instead of concrete. Each kerb avoided 25 kgCO₂ compared with the concrete baseline. [2]

Initiative_Name: Set operational-energy and embodied-carbon targets for new construction and major refurbishment
Title: McDonald’s UK Net-Zero Restaurant
Narrative:
QSR: Operational and embodied-carbon targets – McDonald’s Market Drayton
The design combined on-site renewable generation with product-level material substitutions: two wind turbines and 92 m² of solar generate 60,000 kWh per year, while sheep-wool insulation, recycled-appliance cladding and recycled-plastic kerbs reduce construction impacts. The restaurant was built to the UKGBC net-zero construction framework and used as a blueprint for future freehold new builds. [1]

Cross-sector: Performance targets – Entopia Building
The project set quantified design targets before procurement, including an 85% reduction in energy demand, an expected 80% whole-life carbon saving and embodied carbon of 408 kgCO₂e/m², then used deep retrofit and structural retention to pursue them. [2]

Initiative_Name: Apply carbon criteria at capital-project investment and design gates
Title: McDonald’s UK Net-Zero Restaurant
Narrative:
QSR: Carbon criteria at design approval – McDonald’s Market Drayton
Design approval selected a defined package of on-site renewables and lower-carbon materials rather than leaving sustainability requirements to later procurement. The approved specification included two wind turbines, 92 m² of solar panels, British sheep-wool insulation, 250 m² of recycled-appliance cladding and more than 1,000 lower-carbon recycled-plastic kerbs, creating a repeatable blueprint for future restaurants. [1]

Method Benchmark: Whole-life carbon decision gates – RICS
The RICS standard provides a consistent basis for comparing design options across product, construction, use and end-of-life stages before capital approval, enabling carbon performance to be assessed alongside cost and technical requirements. [2]

Initiative_Name: Require EPDs or product-specific carbon data for priority materials and equipment
Title: McDonald’s UK Net-Zero Restaurant
Narrative:
QSR: Product-specific material selection – McDonald’s Market Drayton
McDonald’s specified named material substitutions with measurable quantities: 250 m² of cladding made from recycled IT and white goods, British sheep wool instead of man-made insulation, and more than 1,000 kerbs made from over 200,000 recycled bottles. Each kerb was reported to avoid 25 kgCO₂ versus a concrete equivalent. [1]

Method Benchmark: Product and EPD evidence – RICS
The RICS whole-life carbon method prioritises product-specific environmental data when available, allowing procurement teams to compare material and equipment options using declared product impacts rather than generic category averages. [2]

Initiative_Name: Prioritise refurbishment, reuse and adaptation before new construction
Title: UKGBC Entopia Building Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Deep retrofit instead of replacement – Entopia Building
Retaining and adapting the existing building reduced energy demand by 85%, delivered an expected 80% whole-life carbon saving and retained the original structure, avoiding about 60% of embodied carbon. [1]

Cross-sector: Adaptive reuse and structural retention – UC Davis Walker Hall
Retaining 75% of the structure, combined with lower-carbon materials, reduced embodied carbon by 57%, diverted 86% of construction waste and avoided about 700 tCO₂e. [2]

Initiative_Name: Require component reuse and material recovery in building and fit-out projects
Title: UKGBC Timber Square Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Structural and component reuse – Timber Square
Reusing about 80% of the original structure by volume saved 7,300 tCO₂; reclaimed floor tiles saved 1,362 tCO₂e and reused steel beams saved 276 tCO₂e. [1]

Restaurants: Circular fit-out and component reuse – Apricity, London
Reusing existing floors, furniture, staircase timber and skirting boards reduced fit-out emissions by 40% compared with a standard restaurant fit-out. [2]

Initiative_Name: Specify lower-carbon and responsibly sourced construction materials
Title: McDonald’s UK Net-Zero Restaurant
Narrative:
QSR: Lower-carbon construction materials – McDonald’s Market Drayton
The restaurant substituted several conventional materials: 250 m² of standard cladding was replaced with panels made from recycled IT and white goods, man-made insulation was replaced with British sheep wool, and more than 1,000 concrete kerbs were replaced with recycled-plastic units made from 182 bottles each. The kerbs reduce emissions by 25 kgCO₂ per unit versus concrete. [1]

Materials Benchmark: Paint carbon disclosure – Dulux
Product EPDs and carbon data allow paint specifications to be compared using product-specific embodied-carbon evidence; recycled paint options contain 35% recycled paint content. [2]

Materials Benchmark: Carpet tile – Interface Heuga 580 II
The carpet tile reports 3.53 kgCO₂e/m² cradle-to-gate embodied carbon, 77% recycled content and a 15-year warranty, with take-back through the ReEntry scheme. [3]

Materials Benchmark: Insulation – Knauf Rocksilk Flexible Slab
The product EPD reports approximately 1.75 kgCO₂e/m² for production stages A1–A3 for the declared flexible-slab unit. [4]

Initiative_Name: Specify durability, repairability, modularity and supplier take-back for capital equipment
Title: Energy Technology List Whitbread Refrigeration Case
Narrative:
Hotels & Restaurants: Modular refrigerated equipment – Whitbread Oxford Beefeater
Whitbread’s all-electric “Kitchen of the Future” replaced traditional undercounter cabinets, which required more space and slower ingredient access, with Adande VCS2 and VCR2 modular drawers at key kitchen stations. Each drawer can operate as chilled or frozen storage, reusable worktops and heat shields reduce replacement waste, and energy monitors at Oxford and Reading established the baseline; the trial confirmed 46% lower refrigeration energy, 13% more gastronorm capacity and about 7 seconds saved per opening, equal to roughly 4 staff hours per kitchen per day, alongside lower meat shrinkage and easier cleaning. [1]

Initiative_Name: Design buildings and fit-outs for adaptability, disassembly and material recovery
Title: UKGBC JLL Manchester Fit-Out Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Adaptable and demountable fit-out – JLL Manchester
A fit-out designed for reuse and reconfiguration achieved 38% lower upfront embodied carbon, reused more than 500 items, made 90% of the floorplate reconfigurable and saved £40,000 through second-hand furniture. [1]

Cross-sector: Design for disassembly and reuse – Timber Square
Reusing about 80% of the original structure saved 7,300 tCO₂ and established recoverable component strategies for future building changes. [2]

Initiative_Name: Commission new buildings and major refurbishments against designed operational performance
Title: Optimised Radisson Blu Case Study
Narrative:
Hotels: Operational commissioning and continuous recommissioning – Radisson Blu
The hotel used its existing submeters and Trend BEMS to collect half-hourly data, identify anomalies and coordinate HVAC, boilers, a 285 kW bio-oil CHP, an absorption chiller and electric chillers that had previously been commissioned separately. Ongoing remote monitoring and repeated retuning reduced total energy by 30%, electricity by 17% and gas by 41%, with under 12-month payback. [1]

Hotels: Existing-building commissioning – Hotel Monaco, Washington DC
The project combined commissioning with targeted efficiency upgrades rather than a single equipment replacement, addressing operating faults and building-system performance. Annual energy use fell 28% and water use 41%, while guest-room temperature complaints fell 11%, linking technical savings with guest comfort. [2]

Initiative_Name: Apply verified energy-efficiency criteria when replacing kitchen equipment
Title: Energy Technology List Greene King Case
Narrative:
Pubs: Verified efficient refrigeration – Greene King Punch and Judy
Greene King used the Energy Technology List as a procurement screen, replacing 8 older mixed-manufacturer double-door bottle coolers with ETL-listed Rhino units selected for rapid pull-down, efficient components and lower energy use. Consumption fell from 4.71 kWh to 0.81 kWh per unit per day, saving about £2,500 per year; reported fan life increased from about 4 to nearly 8 years. [1]

Contract Catering Benchmark: Efficient equipment selection – Carbon Trust
The sector study recommends using verified efficiency criteria at equipment specification, supported by sub-metering to confirm operating performance and shared-investment models where the caterer operates equipment but the client controls capital budgets. This allows lower-energy kitchen equipment to be selected and its savings assigned between the parties. [2]

Initiative_Name: Assess the feasibility of hydrogen-ready kitchen equipment
Title: National Gas Metering Hydrogen Kitchen Case
Narrative:
Commercial Kitchens: Hydrogen-powered kitchen prototype – National Gas Metering
A working industrial kitchen was developed and tested entirely on hydrogen, demonstrating equipment operation and food-quality performance before wider infrastructure investment. [1]

Initiative_Name: Apply environmental-performance criteria when selecting leased sites
Title: Better Buildings Partnership York House Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Environmental criteria for occupied buildings – York House
The landlord and occupier converted broad environmental aims into operating criteria by forming an Environmental Management Group, assigning responsibilities, installing automatic 15-minute energy monitoring and creating an annual Environmental Action Plan. Separating landlord-controlled common-area and HVAC loads from occupier-controlled loads helped identify accountable actions, reducing annual energy by 1.1 million kWh and saving £63,000 and 416 tCO₂. [1]

Initiative_Name: Apply energy and carbon criteria to lease renewals and franchise onboarding
Title: Trane Wendy’s HVAC Case Study
Narrative:
QSR Franchise: Performance criteria at onboarding – Wendy’s
Wendy’s compared two rebuilt restaurants: the control retained two high-efficiency rooftop units plus dedicated make-up air, while the upgraded design paired lower-airflow kitchen hoods with Trane Voyager rooftop units using eFlex variable-speed compressors. Total energy fell 24% at the upgraded site versus 13% at the control over 8 months, and the equipment package became a standard option for new company and franchise locations. [1]

Leased Buildings: Energy criteria at renewal – York House
The landlord and occupier created a shared baseline using automatic 15-minute monitoring, separated each party’s controlled loads and agreed an Environmental Action Plan with named actions and responsibilities. The programme reduced annual energy by 1.1 million kWh, saving £63,000 and 416 tCO₂. [2]

Initiative_Name: Include green performance, data and cooperation clauses in leases and franchise agreements
Title: Better Buildings Partnership York House Case
Narrative:
Leased Buildings: Green cooperation clauses – York House
The landlord and occupier established a formal Environmental Management Group, named responsible representatives and maintained an annual Environmental Action Plan supported by shared 15-minute energy data. This governance structure turned cooperation commitments into tracked actions, reducing landlord-controlled energy by 32% and occupier-controlled energy by 9%. [1]

Lease Benchmark: Green data and cooperation clauses – Better Buildings Partnership
Model clauses provide practical wording for energy-data sharing, metering, renewable procurement and cooperation on environmental improvements, clarifying what information must be shared and how both parties approve and implement actions. [2]

Initiative_Name: Collect and quality-check energy and emissions data from leased, tenanted and franchised sites
Title: Better Buildings Partnership York House Case
Narrative:
Leased Buildings: Shared energy-data controls – York House
Automatic meters recorded energy at 15-minute intervals and the landlord and occupier separated common-area and central-HVAC loads from tenant-controlled consumption, replacing a single undifferentiated building total with accountable datasets. The shared monitoring and action plan supported a 1.1 million kWh annual reduction, £63,000 saving and 416 tCO₂ reduction. [1]

Initiative_Name: Secure rights and approval routes for environmental improvements in leased sites
Title: Better Buildings Partnership York House Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Landlord-occupier approval routes – York House
A formal Environmental Management Group gave landlord and occupier representatives a route to review performance, assign responsibilities and approve an annual Environmental Action Plan using shared 15-minute energy data. Coordinated building and operational changes contributed to 32% lower landlord-controlled energy and 9% lower occupier-controlled energy. [1]

Food & Beverage / Leased Site: Green lease rights – The Coffee House
At a 10-year lease renewal, the tenant and university landlord added utility-data sharing and provisions covering lighting, windows and HVAC so identified improvements could be approved and implemented. The supporting audit identified 12% electricity and 32% gas reduction potential with 2.9-year payback. [2]

Initiative_Name: Enable renewable electricity procurement under lease and franchise arrangements
Title: GreenPark / Energy & Carbon Management Hotel Operator Case
Narrative:
Hotels: Renewable electricity procurement – UK national hotel operator
A national hotel operator moved 75% of electricity demand to certified renewable supply backed by REGOs, contributing to a 22% reduction in total energy consumption and an estimated £1.1 million annual saving. [1]

Hotels: 100% renewable electricity procurement – RIU Hotels Spain
A long-term contract supplies about 70 GWh per year of 100% renewable electricity to 27 hotels and more than 11,000 rooms, avoiding 30,000 tCO₂ per year. [2]

Initiative_Name: Agree landlord-tenant decarbonisation plans with actions, funding and accountability
Title: Better Buildings Partnership York House Case
Narrative:
Cross-sector: Funded landlord-tenant decarbonisation plan – York House
The landlord and occupier built a common evidence base through automatic 15-minute monitoring, formed an Environmental Management Group and assigned actions through an annual plan, enabling responsibilities and benefits to be split between the parties. The programme reduced annual energy by 1.1 million kWh, saving £63,000 and avoiding 416 tCO₂. [1]

Cross-sector: Green lease and funded refurbishment plan – Hollywood House
A green lease and memorandum of understanding allocated the scope of works, capital contributions, savings and payback responsibilities for a £3.2 million refurbishment, converting cooperation into a funded delivery plan. The completed works reduced energy by 45%, carbon by 55% and water use by 55%. [2]

Initiative_Name: Set and monitor energy-performance standards for franchisees
Title: U.S. DOE Wendy’s Franchisee Case
Narrative:
QSR Franchise: Energy-performance standards – Wendy’s Carlisle LLC
Applying leading-edge HVAC and kitchen technologies reduced energy use by 21% across 159 restaurants; 47 franchisees representing 2,170 restaurants committed to a 20% reduction per transaction over 10 years. [1]

QSR Network: Green restaurant standards – McDonald’s China
Scaling LEED restaurant design standards across more than 5,000 certified locations by May 2026 standardised lower-impact materials and energy-efficient building systems across the network. [2]

Initiative_Name: Complete an Energy Health Check
Title: Source: JRP Solutions, ESOS energy audit and compliance - BMI Healthcare case study (consultancy/supplier source, unofficial)

Initiative_Name: Upgrade to LED lighting with optimised design and controls
Title: Source: SaveMoneyCutCarbon, Greene King distribution centre LED case study (installer/supplier source, unofficial)
Narrative: Travelodge retrofitted LED across 388 UK hotels between 2017 and 2020, reported to save c.20.2 GWh a year (c.52 MWh per hotel); Greene King's Abingdon distribution centre retrofit saves nearly £15,000 a year.

Title: Source: Whitbread PLC, 'First all-electric Premier Inn hotel powered entirely by renewables opens in Swindon', 16 October 2023 (official, first-party)

Title: Source: Punch Pubs & Co, Sustainability: Planet (official, first-party)
Narrative: Greene King installed 13,052 cellar and dispense control units, reported to save 22 million kWh in year one at c.14-month payback; Punch Pubs cut site energy 8-11% across 300+ pubs with the same class of controls.

Initiative_Name: Replace gas-fired heating and catering equipment with electric alternatives
Title: Source: Mitchells & Butlers plc, Respect for the Planet, and Annual Report 2025 (official, first-party)
Narrative: Mitchells & Butlers electrified 100 kitchens in FY2025 (from 60) and took 24 sites fully off gas (from 5); Whitbread defines a low-carbon room as no gas or LPG plus REGO-backed power, reaching 2,300 by March 2026.

Initiative_Name: Install on-site solar PV
Title: Source: The Morning Advertiser, 'Marston's installs solar at 120 pubs to secure energy prices', 12 May 2025 (trade press reporting a company announcement, third-party)
Narrative: Marston's installed solar at 120 pubs for £5.4m financed by Atrato, c.30,000 kWh per site meeting 15-20% of pub demand and 600 tCO2e in year one; St Austell Brewery reports 40% on-site generation at Hare Brewery.

Initiative_Name: Install voltage optimisation equipment
Title: Source: Whitbread PLC, Sustainability Report 2025/26, published 29 April 2026 (official, first-party, dated)

Title: Sources

Initiative_Name: Optimise heating controls
Title: Source: Stonegate Group, FY25 circular economy and sustainability release (official, first-party; confirmed live August 2026)
Narrative: Stonegate reports energy down 18% since 2023 across c.4,000 pubs, attributed substantially to optimisation and smart controls rather than plant replacement; Whitbread validates control changes against live smart-meter data under ISO 50001.

Initiative_Name: Connect sites to low-carbon heat networks or solar thermal
